data.body_html:
August in Marbella is synonymous with blazing sun, high temperatures, and the Mediterranean at its warmest. For anyone planning a Marbella boat rental in August 2027, understanding the weather is key to a comfortable and safe day on the water. This guide covers everything you need to know: average temperatures, sea conditions, wind patterns, and practical tips for beating the heat. Whether you're booking a 2-hour spin from Puerto Banús or a full-day charter along the Costa del Sol, being prepared makes all the difference.

Average Temperatures and Sunshine Hours

August is Marbella's hottest month. Daytime highs average 31°C, but it's not unusual to see the mercury hit 34–36°C in the shade. Night-time lows hover around 22°C, so evenings remain balmy. Sunshine is almost guaranteed: you can expect 10–11 hours of clear skies daily. The UV index peaks at 9, meaning unprotected skin can burn in under 20 minutes. Sea surface temperature reaches 24°C, rising to 26°C in shallow coves like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. This makes swimming and water sports exceptionally pleasant.

Wind and Sea State

The prevailing wind in August is the Levante, blowing from the east at 10–15 knots. This creates a gentle chop on the open sea, generally 1–2 on the Douglas scale (waves 0.1–1.0 metres). It's perfectly manageable for all boats in our fleet, from the compact Mariah SX21 to the 29-metre Ferretti 94. Occasionally, a Poniente (west wind) brings cooler, drier air and flatter seas. Our skippers monitor forecasts and will adjust the route to sheltered bays if needed. The sea is typically calmest in the morning, making early departures a smart choice.

Best Times to Cruise

To avoid the fiercest heat, plan your charter for either the morning (10:00–14:00) or late afternoon (17:00–sunset). Midday sun between 14:00 and 16:00 is intense, but easily managed with shaded areas, cold drinks, and a swim stop. A full-day charter from 10:00 to 18:00 works well, with a lunch break at a beach club like Nikki Beach or Playa Padre. Our fleet includes boats with flybridges, biminis, and cabin spaces for shade. All charters include unlimited water, soft drinks, beer, cava, and light snacks to keep you refreshed.

What to Wear and Pack

Lightweight, breathable fabrics are essential. Think linen, cotton, or quick-dry synthetics. A swimsuit under your clothes is a must. Bring a wide-brimmed hat, polarised sunglasses, and a light long-sleeve shirt for sun protection. Non-slip boat shoes or bare feet are fine. A thin windbreaker or hoodie is useful for the evening breeze. Don't forget reef-safe sunscreen (SPF 50+), lip balm with SPF, and a towel. If you're prone to seasickness, consider taking medication the night before – though the sea is generally calm, the heat can amplify nausea.

Popular August Destinations

From Puerto Banús, you can head east to Marbella's Golden Mile and Cabopino, or west to Estepona and Sotogrande. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés offer sheltered coves with crystal-clear water. The coastline near La Concha mountain provides some shade in the late afternoon. For a longer trip, the 24-metre Mangusta 80 can reach Gibraltar in under an hour. The Mangusta 80 includes a free jet ski, adding fun to your swim stops. All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, making logistics simple.

Staying Safe in the Heat

Heat exhaustion is a real risk in August. Symptoms include headache, dizziness, and nausea. To prevent it: drink water every 20 minutes, avoid alcohol in the middle of the day, and use the boat's shaded areas. Our skippers are trained to recognise heat-related issues and will adjust the itinerary if needed. The Azimut 58 Flybridge offers a spacious, shaded saloon with air conditioning. For smaller boats like the Speedboat or Red Tide, the bimini top provides essential cover. Remember that the sea breeze can mask how much sun you're getting – reapply sunscreen every two hours.

Booking Tips for August

August is peak season, so availability is tight. Book at least 2–3 weeks in advance. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours, all inclusive. The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) requires a minimum 4-hour booking at €4,719, which includes a jet ski. For other boats, pricing is on request via WhatsApp. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and 21% IVA. Contact us via WhatsApp for the best availability and last-minute deals.
